enhanced.fullText:
The Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA), codified at 42 U.S.C. §§ 2000gg through 2000gg-2, became effective June 27, 2023, establishing comprehensive federal protections for pregnant workers and those experiencing childbirth or related medical conditions. This landmark legislation applies to higher education institutions with 15 or more employees, including faculty, staff, and student workers.

Under 42 U.S.C. § 2000gg(7), covered entities include public and private universities, community colleges, and educational service organizations. The Act's core mandate requires institutions to provide reasonable accommodations for known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions, unless doing so would impose an undue hardship as defined in 42 U.S.C. § 2000gg(5).

Key provisions under 42 U.S.C. § 2000gg-1 prohibit five specific unlawful employment practices: (1) failing to make reasonable accommodations for known limitations unless undue hardship exists; (2) forcing employees to accept accommodations without engaging in the interactive process; (3) denying employment opportunities because accommodation needs exist; (4) requiring leave when other reasonable accommodations are available; and (5) retaliating against employees for requesting or using accommodations.

Reasonable accommodations in higher education contexts may include modified work schedules for faculty, ergonomic furniture, temporary assignment modifications, additional breaks, remote work options, or temporary reassignment of certain duties. The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) enforces the PWFA under 42 U.S.C. § 2000gg-2, with jurisdiction to investigate complaints, issue determinations, and pursue litigation.

Violations may result in monetary damages, reinstatement, injunctive relief, and attorney's fees under the same enforcement mechanisms as Title VII. The EEOC's interpretive guidance, expected under 29 CFR Part 1636, will provide additional implementation details for covered employers.

Higher education institutions must establish interactive processes, train supervisors on accommodation procedures, maintain confidential medical information protocols, and ensure non-retaliation policies encompass PWFA protections. Unlike the Pregnancy Discrimination Act's anti-discrimination focus, the PWFA creates affirmative accommodation obligations similar to the Americans with Disabilities Act framework.

Institutions should review existing policies, update employee handbooks, train human resources personnel, and establish clear procedures for processing accommodation requests. The Act's broad definition of "related medical conditions" includes lactation, fertility treatments, pregnancy loss, and other reproductive health conditions, requiring comprehensive policy coverage.
enhanced.summary: The PWFA requires higher education institutions with 15+ employees to provide reasonable accommodations for pregnancy-related limitations, prohibits retaliation, and mandates interactive processes for accommodation requests.
enhanced.requirements:
## Accommodation Obligations
- Provide reasonable accommodations for known pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical condition limitations per 42 U.S.C. § 2000gg-1(1)
- Engage in interactive process before implementing accommodations
- Demonstrate undue hardship through individualized assessment if denying requests

## Prohibited Practices
- Denying employment opportunities based on accommodation needs
- Forcing employees to take leave when other accommodations are available
- Retaliating against employees for requesting or using accommodations per 42 U.S.C. § 2000gg-1(5)

## Policy Implementation
- Establish written accommodation procedures and request processes
- Train supervisors and HR personnel on PWFA requirements
- Update employee handbooks and anti-discrimination policies
- Maintain confidential medical documentation systems

## Coverage Requirements
- Apply protections to all employees including faculty, staff, and student workers
- Cover temporary, part-time, and probationary employees under institutional employment
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No specific federal reporting requirements under PWFA. Institutions must maintain accommodation request records, document interactive processes, and preserve relevant employment records per EEOC guidelines for potential investigations or compliance reviews.
